summary: Grouped settings that either apply immediately or are saved together — never both in one panel.
useWhen: the user configures preferences, feature flags or account options
the settings are grouped and the groups are worth naming
structure: Named groups, separated by Divider, each with a heading.
One SettingRow per setting: label and description on the left, control on the right, wired together by the row.
For save-on-submit panels, a save bar that appears only when something is dirty, with save and discard.
Tabs for panels large enough that a single scroll is unreasonable — but never with unsaved changes hidden behind an inactive tab.

A setting used from outside the app — an API key, a webhook, a CLI — shows how to use it as CodeSnippets under a sentence saying what each is for: a command as `single`, a request as `multi`, each with its own `label` and `copyLabel`, and a command named in a description as `inline`.

loading.must: Show the groups and their labels with the controls disabled, rather than an empty panel.
loading.why: the shape of the settings is known before their values are; showing it makes the wait legible

empty.must: A group with nothing in it for this account states why — a plan limit, a permission — rather than being hidden.
empty.why: a silently absent setting reads as a missing feature, and generates support tickets

error.must: Revert the control to its previous value, show an Alert naming the setting that failed, and keep the rest of the panel usable.
error.why: a Toggle left in the new position after a failed save is a lie about the server's state

partial.must: When a batched save partially fails, keep the successful values and mark only the failed rows dirty again.
partial.why: reverting everything discards changes the server accepted

requires: a label on every control — the row's visible text, wired up, not just placed beside it
the description associated with the control rather than floating next to it, so it is announced with the setting
an announcement when an immediate-apply setting saves; the visual state change is not enough
notes: Toggle for immediate effect, Checkbox for values saved with a submit. Mixing both in one panel means the user cannot tell which is which.

antiPatterns.dont: Toggles that apply immediately alongside a Save button
antiPatterns.why: the switch says the change already happened; the button says it has not

antiPatterns.dont: a destructive setting with no confirmation
antiPatterns.why: "delete this workspace" as a Toggle row is one mis-click

antiPatterns.dont: unsaved changes on an inactive tab
antiPatterns.why: the user is told the form is dirty with nothing on screen that is

antiPatterns.dont: hiding settings the account cannot use
antiPatterns.why: an absent control is indistinguishable from a missing feature
